data.title: UiPath Earns Hold Rating Despite Strong Results and Raised Guidance as Analyst Awaits Clearer AI-Driven Growth Acceleration
data.description:
William Blair analyst Patrick McIlwee has reiterated their neutral stance on PATH stock, giving a Hold rating today.

Patrick McIlwee has given his Hold rating due to a combination of factors, starting with UiPath’s operational performance. The company delivered stronger-than-expected results in annual recurring revenue, sales, and profitability, and management modestly raised full-year guidance, signaling improving fundamentals and steady customer spend trends.

At the same time, he views the current share price as already reflecting much of this progress, with UiPath trading at a notable premium to similar software peers despite only modestly higher growth. While he sees upside potential from the increasing integration of AI into larger deals and a seemingly smooth CFO/COO transition, he prefers to wait for clearer evidence that AI-driven initiatives will materially accelerate revenue before taking a more constructive stance, leading to a Hold recommendation.

data.title: Upstart Maintains Fair Valuation as Origination Trends Stabilize; Nance Reiterates Hold Rating and $39 Price Target
data.description:
Analyst Will Nance from Goldman Sachs maintained a Hold rating on Upstart Holdings and keeping the price target at $39.00.

Will Nance has given his Hold rating due to a combination of factors, including origination trends that now align more closely with market expectations. Upstart’s August loan originations showed a solid acceleration, putting third-quarter volumes roughly in line with, or slightly ahead of, current Street forecasts, which supports a more neutral stance rather than a clear bullish call.

At the same time, the Upstart Macro Index remains elevated versus historical norms, indicating default rates that are modestly higher than average and tempering the risk-reward profile. Given that recent performance does not markedly surpass the strong second quarter and that credit conditions remain only cautiously constructive, Nance keeps his price target unchanged at $39 and views the shares as fairly valued at present.
